_source: Ministry of Education / Curriculum Development Centre, Zambia — Principles of Accounts Scheme of Work, Form 1, Terms 1-3 (2026), as prepared by a serving teacher against the official CDC Principles of Accounts syllabus (each entry cites the syllabus page it is drawn from, e.g. 'Syllabus p.30'). No separate full syllabus document was available for this subject/form at ingestion time, so topic, sub-topic, competency and learning-objective text is reconstructed from the scheme's own Topic/Subtopic/Specific Competence/Content/Learning Activities columns. The source document's teacher name, TS number and school name have been removed — this file contains no identifying information about who prepared the source scheme, per this app's standing content policy of crediting only CDC/Ministry of Education. Several specific-competence codes (1.1.1.1, 1.3.2.1, 1.4.2.1, 1.5.1.1) each cover multiple consecutive weeks/parts of the same skill (e.g. 1.5.1.1 spans six weeks covering different Books of Prime Entry) — these are kept as one competency with multiple learning objectives rather than split, matching how the source scheme presents them. Weeks used for Revisions/Reporting, Mid-Term Test, Revision & Integration and End-of-Term Test carry no new topic content and are omitted.

subject.name: Principles of Accounts
subject.description: Ordinary Level Secondary Principles of Accounts syllabus, Form 1-4 (Curriculum Development Centre).

grade.name: Form 1
grade.phase: Secondary — the source scheme itself uses "Form 1" for this level under the 2023 CBC.

sub_topics.name: 1.1.1 Introduction to Principles of Accounts
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: meaning of Accounting and book-keeping demonstrated accordingly.

competencies.description: Demonstrate knowledge of Principles of Accounts

learning_objectives.description: Explaining Accounting, Principles of Accounts, and book-keeping, and discussing the relationship between book-keeping and accounting
Stating the importance of Principles of Accounts and identifying career prospects (Accountant, Accounts Clerk, Cashier, Auditor, Finance Manager, Book Keeper, Bursar, Financial Controller)

sub_topics.name: 1.1.2 Users of Accounting Information
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: users of Accounting Information described accordingly.

learning_objectives.description: Explaining accounting information (Income Statement, Statement of Financial Position, list of payables and receivables)

Describing internal users (business owners, shareholders, employees, internal auditors) and external users (customers, suppliers, potential shareholders, general public, lenders, government, external auditors)

sub_topics.name: 1.1.3 Accounting Terminologies
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: Accounting Terminologies used correctly.

learning_objectives.description: Outlining and explaining accounting terminologies (Book-keeping, Business Transaction, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Inventory, Assets, Liabilities)

sub_topics.name: 1.1.4 Accounting Concepts
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: Accounting Concepts applied accordingly.

competencies.description: Apply Accounting Concepts in recording Business Transactions

learning_objectives.description: Outlining accounting concepts (Going Concern, Accruals/Matching, Consistency, Prudence, Business Entity, Realization, Cost, Objectivity, Materiality, Duality, Substance over Form, Periodical) and applying them to given scenarios

sub_topics.name: 1.2.1 Ethics in Accountancy
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: Ethics in Accountancy applied accordingly; roles of the Accountancy Regulatory body demonstrated accordingly.

competencies.description: Demonstrate understanding of the roles of the Accountancy Regulatory body in Zambia

learning_objectives.description: Identifying and explaining ethics in accountancy (Integrity, Honesty, Discipline, Trustworthy, Accountability) and effects of non-adherence
Describing the roles of ZICA (Zambia Institute of Chartered Accountants) in regulating the accounting profession

sub_topics.name: 1.3.1 Types of Business Transactions
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: knowledge of Business Transactions demonstrated accordingly.

learning_objectives.description: Explaining the meaning of business transactions and identifying/classifying types (Cash, Credit and Contra)

sub_topics.name: 1.3.2 Accounting Equation
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: elements of the Accounting Equation explained accordingly; Accounting Equation applied accordingly to determine financial position.

competencies.description: Use Accounting Equation to determine financial position

learning_objectives.description: Explaining the accounting equation (Assets = Capital + Liabilities) and classifying items as assets, capital or liabilities
Illustrating effects of transactions on the Accounting Equation and applying it to determine financial position

sub_topics.name: 1.4.1 Classes of Accounts
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: Ledger Accounts classified accordingly.

learning_objectives.description: Explaining the Ledger and Ledger Accounts, and identifying/categorising classes of accounts (Nominal, Real and Personal)

sub_topics.name: 1.4.2 Principle of Double Entry
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: steps in the double entry system explained accordingly; Business Transactions recorded accordingly using the double entry system; Ledger Accounts balanced off accordingly.

competencies.description: Apply double entry system in recording business transactions

learning_objectives.description: Explaining double entry and identifying debit and credit sides of an account
Recording business transactions using the double entry system in appropriate ledger accounts, and practising posting entries
Outlining the steps in balancing off a ledger account and balancing off ledger accounts using practical examples

sub_topics.name: 1.4.3 Types of Ledgers
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: Business Transactions recorded in the appropriate Ledger accordingly.

competencies.description: Record Business Transactions in the appropriate Ledger

learning_objectives.description: Identifying and explaining types of Ledgers (General/Nominal, Payables/Purchases Ledger, Receivables/Sales Ledger) and classifying accounts accordingly

sub_topics.name: 1.5.1 Types of Books of Prime Entry
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: Business Transactions recorded in the Books of Prime Entry accordingly, posted to the Ledger, and the Trial Balance extracted accordingly.

competencies.description: Record Business Transactions in the Books of Prime Entry

learning_objectives.description: Identifying and explaining the Purchases Day Book and Purchases Returns Day Book
Identifying and explaining the Sales Day Book and Sales Returns Day Book/Returns Inwards Book
Stating and matching source documents for each Book of Prime Entry (Original/Duplicate Invoice, Debit Note/Original Credit Note, Duplicate Debit/Credit Note)
Entering business transactions in the Subsidiary Books (Date, Details, Source Document Number, Subtotal, Amount)
Posting transactions from the Books of Prime Entry to the Ledger
Extracting the Trial Balance from ledger account balances and checking its arithmetic accuracy
